UNC–Chapel Hill · Class of 2027

I study patterns in fluids, light, and data.

I’m Yuanzhuo Sun, an undergraduate in Statistics and Data Science with a minor in Mathematics. My work sits between experiments and computation: using optical measurements, mathematical models, and scientific code to understand density-stratified flows.

01

Current focus

Optical inference of density stratification

Recovering physical structure from curved laser paths in miscible Hele-Shaw flows.

Research

Measuring what the eye cannot see directly.

Density gradients bend light. That simple fact turns an optical path into a measurement: trace the beam carefully, connect image coordinates to the experimental geometry, and fit a physical model to infer the fluid structure that produced it.

I work with Prof. Richard M. McLaughlin and collaborators on experiments in miscible stratified flow, with particular interest in overturning, interfaces, and reliable image-to-physics pipelines.

02 / 04

Research project · 2026

Applied mathematics + experiments

Optical Inference of Density Stratification in Miscible Hele-Shaw Flow

Built a single-camera workflow that follows refracted laser paths through a stratified tank, calibrates pixels against known geometry, and fits the observed trajectory to a physical model. The system supports targeted regions of interest and exclusion zones for difficult experimental images.

  • Optical diagnostics
  • Numerical fitting
  • Computer vision
  • Uncertainty-aware calibration

Instrumentation

Two-chamber injection control

A synchronized two-pump system that combines fluid streams through a mixing chamber to produce designed density profiles for tank experiments.

Communication

Posters and work in progress

Presented undergraduate research through UNC’s Office for Undergraduate Research in 2026. Two related manuscripts are currently in preparation.

Beyond the lab

Statistics, mathematics, and community.

At UNC–Chapel Hill, I study Statistics and Data Science alongside a Mathematics minor. I’m especially drawn to problems where physical intuition and computation have to agree—not just approximately, but in a way that survives contact with an actual experiment.

Outside research, I serve as President of the Badminton Club at UNC–Chapel Hill and compete in local tournaments. I was the Mixed Doubles D runner-up at the 2026 Duke Open.
